Sea ice most plausibly causes the change in net surface shortwave flux (option A). This rests on physical reasoning rather than anything the data can show.

The two variables are weakly correlated (r ≈ 0.14), so the data alone can't settle the direction. Sea ice has a high albedo, so more ice reflects more sunlight and changes the net shortwave absorbed at the surface. Shortwave flux changes, on the other hand, would affect ice only slowly through melting.

ANSWER: A
